## Broken Link Checking

[`.github/workflows/link-check.yml`](.github/workflows/link-check.yml) builds the app, runs it against the seeded CI database, and uses [`linkinator`](https://github.com/JustinBeckwith/linkinator) to recursively crawl the **public** surface from `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Any non-skipped internal link that returns a 4xx/5xx fails the workflow (and therefore the PR check). The full JSON report is uploaded as a build artifact on every run.

External hosts are deliberately out of scope here so PRs don't break on third-party outages — those are covered by the separate weekly external-link job (SYS-616).

Exclusions live in [`linkinator.config.json`](linkinator.config.json) at the repo root: add a per-URL or per-domain regular expression to the `skip` array to stop a link being checked. The first entry (`^https?://(?!127\.0\.0\.1:3000)`) is what scopes the crawl to internal links; leave it in place and add new exclusions alongside it. The authenticated `src/app/footy/**` admin surface is not yet crawled (it needs the mock-auth cookie and the programmatic API — a follow-up).

To run it locally, start a production build on port 3000 and point the script at it:

```shell
op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build
npm run start:ci &
npm run linkcheck
```

Implemented SYS-572 v1 (public-surface broken-link checking in CI).

**New files**
- `linkinator.config.json` (repo root) — `recurse`, `retry`, `concurrency: 20`, `timeout: 10000`, and `skip: ["^https?://(?!127\\.0\\.0\\.1:3000)"]` which scopes the crawl to internal links only. Kept as pure JSON (not the ticket's jsonc sketch) because linkinator loads it with `JSON.parse` and chokes on comments. Verified the regex skips every external host while leaving `127.0.0.1:3000` links checked.
- `.github/workflows/link-check.yml` — standalone workflow, triggers `push: main` / `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch`. Reuses the `playwright.yml` recipe: GHCR login → `docker compose ... up -d` → wait-for-healthy → `prisma db push` with the `--accept-data-loss` fallback + `reseed` output. Then a `Seed database` step mirroring `e2e/global-setup.ts` (full `seed:ci` only on schema divergence, otherwise `refresh:upcoming-gameday:ci`) → `npm run build` → `npm run start:ci &` + `npx wait-on` → `npx linkinator ... --format json > linkinator-report.json`. linkinator exits non-zero on any non-skipped 4xx/5xx, failing the PR check. Report uploaded `if: always()`; a `failure()`-only step prints the broken links since `--format json` hides them from the log.

**Changed**
- `package.json` — `linkinator@^8.1.0` in devDependencies + a `linkcheck` script (`linkinator http://127.0.0.1:3000 --config linkinator.config.json`). The script means knip sees the binary as used, so no `knip.json` change was needed.
- `package-lock.json` — linkinator dependency tree.
- `README.md` — badge + a "Broken Link Checking" section documenting `linkinator.config.json`'s `skip` array as the exclusion point and how to run it locally.

**Checks:** `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `knip` all exit 0 (the two knip config hints are pre-existing). Smoke-tested linkinator locally: it detects a broken internal link and exits 1.

Not touched — these are explicitly v2 / follow-on in the ticket: the authenticated admin crawl, and deleting `e2e/site-crawl.spec.ts` / `e2e/homepage.links.spec.ts`.

The representative fix is **option 3 — harden the mugshot route so it degrades instead of 500ing** — because it's the only one that changes what a real visitor sees. Today, whenever a blob is missing or Azure hiccups, every game and player page renders broken avatars *and* logs a 500 to Sentry. The link checker just made that visible at scale (1362 references from `/footy/game/*` alone).

What "improve the real site" looks like at the route level:

- **Valid player ⇒ always an image (200).** Read a placeholder that ships with the repo (there's already `src/tests/mocks/data/mugshot.png`; promote a real one to `src/assets/` or `public/`) and return it whenever Azure can't serve a blob — missing secrets, `download()` throws, blob absent, no stream body. The existing "anonymous player ⇒ manofmystery" branch just points at the local placeholder instead of a blob.

## Auto-generating a sitemap

Yes, natively — no dependency needed. Next App Router has file conventions for both:

- **`src/app/sitemap.ts`** — export `default async function sitemap(): Promise<MetadataRoute.Sitemap>`, served at `/sitemap.xml`. It can be `async` and call services to enumerate the dynamic routes the crawl can't discover on its own (`/footy/player/[id]`, `/footy/game/[id]`, per-year table routes). `generateSitemaps()` splits into multiple files only past 50 000 URLs — irrelevant here.
- **`src/app/robots.ts`** — `MetadataRoute.Robots`, served at `/robots.txt`, with a `sitemap: 'https://www.toastboy.co.uk/sitemap.xml'` field.

Don't reach for `next-sitemap` (community postbuild package) — the built-ins cover this and stay in the "fetch on the server" model.

Two things make excluding them the right call rather than a preference:

**1. The premise doesn't hold for those routes.** `/footy/admin/**` and the account pages (`/footy/players`, `/footy/profile`, `/footy/password`, `/footy/deleteaccount`, `/footy/downloadmydata`) don't render a "please sign in" message — their layouts (`src/app/footy/admin/layout.tsx`, `src/app/footy/(authenticated)/layout.tsx`) do a server-side `redirect()` to `/footy/auth/signin?redirect=…` for anyone not logged in. A URL that 307s is inert in a sitemap: Google won't index the source, and Search Console reports it under "Page with redirect". Listing them achieves nothing.

**2. A sitemap isn't "every URL that resolves" — it's "pages with public content I want to rank".** That's Google's actual guidance. A login wall indexed as a search result is a bad result: someone searches, lands on a sign-in form, bounces. And listing paths in `sitemap.xml` that `robots.txt` disallows makes Search Console flag the contradiction ("Sitemap contains URLs blocked by robots.txt"). The nav/crawl is what verifies "every link resolves"; the sitemap is a curated ranking hint.

**The pages that match your description are already included.** `/footy/game/[id]`, `/footy/player/[id]`, `/footy/game` render full content to anonymous visitors and just *add* admin controls when `role === 'admin'` (see `getUserRole()` in the game page) — no redirect, no gate. Those are genuine public content pages and they're in the sitemap.

So the split is: renders public content (even if it shows more when logged in) → in; pure authenticated tool that redirects anon users → out.

The one arguable addition is `/footy/auth/signin` itself (a real 200 page) if you want "toastboy login" discoverable in search — I'd still leave it out as it's not content, but it's defensible. The token pages (`claim/[token]`, `verify/.../[token]`, `response/[token]`) must stay out regardless — per-user and single-use.

Happy to add `/footy/auth/signin` specifically if you want it, but I'd leave the rest excluded.

Building URLs via string concatenation can produce malformed URLs if getPublicBaseUrl() ever includes a trailing slash (e.g. https://example.com/ + /footy → https://example.com//footy) or if callers pass paths without a leading slash. Consider normalizing with the URL constructor (e.g. new URL(path || '/', baseUrl).toString()) and/or trimming exactly one trailing slash from baseUrl.

CI is behaving exactly as designed for v1 — the bad link is in a place the public crawl can't reach.

**Where you put it:** `NavBarNested.tsx` line 174, inside `adminLinks`, right after `/footy/admin/users`. That whole section is gated:

```tsx
{user?.role === 'admin' && (
    ...adminLinks.map(...)
)}
```

**Why the crawl misses it (two independent reasons):**

1. `link-check.yml` crawls **unauthenticated**. `user` is undefined, so the admin `<nav>` section never renders, so `/footy/admin/busted` never appears as an `<a href>` on any page linkinator sees. It found the same 346 public links as before, all 200 → `passed: true`.
2. Even if you handed linkinator that URL directly, `src/app/footy/admin/layout.tsx` does `redirect()` to `/footy/auth/signin?admin=true&…` for non-admins, and linkinator follows redirects and reports the **final** status — 200 (the signin page). A broken admin route resolves to a healthy signin page for an anonymous crawler.

This is precisely the deferred **v2** scope in SYS-572 ("cover the authenticated / admin surface… an unauthenticated crawl gets redirects/401/403 and never sees them") — which needs the programmatic `LinkChecker` sending `Cookie: MOCK_AUTH_COOKIE=admin` on every request.

**To actually exercise v1:** move the bad link to a non-admin part of the nav (the always-rendered `mainLinks`, e.g. next to `/footy/rules`). The next `link-check` run will then fail on it. Then revert.
Presumably some of the invariants can be cached in GitHub cache for the link checker workflow

The only piece worth a cache step is the **Next.js build cache**; everything else is either already cached or not worth the bytes.

## Worth adding: `.next/cache`

```yaml
- name: Cache Next.js build
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
      path: .next/cache
      key: ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}-${{ hashFiles('src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}', 'prisma/schema.prisma') }}
      restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}-
```

Placed after `npm run generate`, before `npm run build`.

Two honest caveats:

- This project builds with **Turbopack** (the `turbopack-*.js` chunks in the crawl output confirm it). Turbopack's persistent cache in `.next/cache` is less mature than webpack's, so the speedup is real but smaller than the "~40%" you'd see on a webpack build.
- `generateBuildId` is `git rev-parse HEAD`, so every commit gets a fresh build ID. That doesn't defeat `.next/cache` (it's module/compile cache, not keyed on build ID), but there's no "identical build, skip entirely" short-circuit.

The same `npm run build` runs in `playwright.yml`, so add the step there too with the **same key** and both workflows share one cache entry.

## Not worth it

| Candidate | Why skip |
|---|---|
| `npm` download cache | Already done — `cache: "npm"` on `setup-node`. |
| `node_modules` (skip `npm ci` on hit) | Real ~30–60s saving, but no other workflow in this repo does it. Diverging only here adds inconsistency and a stale-native-module failure mode — do it repo-wide or not at all. |
| `prisma generate` output | A few seconds; the slow part (engine download) is already in the npm cache. |
| Seeded DB image | It's a *pull* from GHCR (same provider as the runner), not a build. `docker save`/`load` caching would eat a large share of the 10 GB/repo Actions cache for little gain. |
| linkinator / crawl results | The crawl must run fresh every time — that's the whole job. |

Added the `Cache Next.js build` step to both workflows, same key so they share one cache entry:

- **`link-check.yml`** — after `npm run generate`, before GHCR login.
- **`playwright.yml`** — after `npm ci`, before GHCR login.

```yaml
- name: Cache Next.js build
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
      path: .next/cache
      key: ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}-${{ hashFiles('src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}', 'prisma/schema.prisma') }}
      restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}-
```

Both files parse as valid YAML.

One expected wart: `playwright.yml` is a 5-way matrix, so on a fresh key the first leg saves the cache and the other four log a harmless "Cache already exists" warning at save time. Restores are unaffected. If that noise bothers you later, the fix is a separate one-off `build` job that the matrix `needs:`, but that's a bigger restructure than this ticket warrants.
